name: comp-510

frames.best_why: Both months show prices, 14 November is circled and the green cheap nights stand out.
frames.render_note: Calendar is small and centred in a large empty stage, so the price text is barely legible.

tagline: Two-month calendar printing nightly prices under each date.
summary: A tall calendar showing November and December stacked, with a small dollar price beneath every available day. Nights under a hundred dollars are tinted green, days without a price are dimmed and unclickable, and a chosen day fills white.
appearance: Two month blocks share a bordered black panel, each with a centred name, weekday initials and large square day cells. Each available day carries the number above a tiny dollar figure, some in emerald green, and the selected day sits in a solid white circle.
behaviour: Clicking an available day circles it white while hovering fades a light square behind a day. The arrows turn both months together, and days with no price data cannot be pressed at all.
demo_content: November and December 2026 with random nightly prices between $80 and $200; 14 November selected.
search_phrases: calendar showing nightly prices on each day
booking calendar with price per night
two month calendar for travel dates
flight or hotel date price grid
pick a day and see the cost
calendar where low prices stand out
date grid with dollar amounts underneath
use_when: Travellers compare nightly costs before choosing dates, so price needs to sit on the calendar.
avoid_when: Prices are random mock figures created on load, so they are not real and differ on every visit.
customise: The price generator, the 180-day window and the $100 green threshold live in the file; real prices or another highlight rule means editing the source.
weight_why: Two month grids and 180 generated prices; nothing animates.

a11y.note: Day buttons carry the date and price as text, but cheap nights are marked by green colour alone with no words.

issues: Prices are random mock values regenerated on every page load.
Cheap nights are signalled by colour alone, so colour-blind users miss the cue.
The calendar is small in a wide empty stage, making prices hard to read.
The caption credits the calendar library instead of describing the prices.
polish_why: Prices on dates read well in concept, but tiny type and random mock figures hold it back.
title: Pricing Calendar
